sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Aseptic Tubing of Ambient Quick-Cook Tapioca Pearls

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United Kingdom BIT (1993, continued pursuant to UK-EU separation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 October 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as regulated by Executive Decree No. 219 of 12 February 1996 and amended by Law 62 of 2018; AML/CFT framework: Law 23 of 27 May 2015 as amended by Law 70 of 23 October 2019, Law 379 of 13 November 2024, and UAF Resolution No. 002-2020 (Beneficial Ownership Registry). Mandatory UBO registration for all legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations, is governed by the Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva / Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public (Notario Público de la República de Panamá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a Hague Apostille Convention contracting state, effective 2007) or Consular Legalization for non-apostille jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the founding settlor's passport or national ID
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil Registry / National Police / competent passport authority of the settlor's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, then certified Spanish translation by an official Panamanian translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation (Poder de Representación) granted to the Panamanian resident agent or legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin of the settlor, with verified legal capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, and 180-day validity from notarization date

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional reference letter for each founder / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank and independent professional (lawyer/accountant) in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, if requested by the resident agent or Panama Public Registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Existence of the founding corporate entity (if the settlor is a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the settlor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with Spanish translation if not in Spanish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List (US), UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's List of Prohibited Entities (CAOS) issued by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), along with domestic Panamanian AML/CFT risk indicators. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any senior political figure (PEP), requiring validation of source of funds and source of wealth; a 24-month cooling-off criterion applies to domestic PEPs and 12-month to foreign/international PEPs. The resident agent must maintain updated records and file annual confirmations with the UBO Registry.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Online Name Reservation System (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre en Línea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name may be in Spanish or English; if a non-Spanish language is used, a certified Spanish transliteration/translation must be filed. Names must be composed exclusively of Latin alphabet characters (A–Z), Arabic numerals, ampersands (&), periods, commas, and hyphens. The name must contain the distinguishing corporate element 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'FIP'. Names that are merely denominative without any distinctive element, or that are vulgar, contrary to public order, or misleadingly similar to existing registered names, are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection (negative name clearance), the applicant or its resident agent may file a written 'reconsideración' petition with the Director General of the Public Registry within five (5) business days of notification, offering alternatively a modified name. If the Director General denies the reconsideration, the applicant may pursue an administrative remedy before the Civil and Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice within two (2) months of the denial, or may submit a completely new name application without prejudice. A reserved name may be extended for a single additional term of thirty (30) days by paying the applicable extension tariff to the Public Registry before the initial reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible for the statutory registered office of a Private Interest Foundation engaged in physical manufacturing activities. A real physical address in the Republic of Panama, maintained by the resident agent or a Panamanian law firm, is required for service of process and governmental notifications. The PIF must maintain at this address (or at the registered agent's office) any statutory records, membership books, and accounting records. For an active ISIC 1030 food manufacturing business, a virtual office cannot satisfy the commercial substance expectations of the tax and customs authorities, and such arrangement will heighten reporting requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 8% annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the UAF, Dirección General de Impuestos (DGI), or municipal authorities, given the low-risk tier of the canned food processing industry and the PIF's non-public UBO regime. The probability rises to 20% if the PIF holds physical equipment, inventories, or employees in Panama without a formal operating branch or business license.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary UBO/KYC screening and sanctions database trawls (OFAC, UN, EU, CAOS, and PEP lists) for settlor and all named beneficiaries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for enhanced due diligence package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and reservation fee (30-day reservation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per the Public Registry Name Reservation Fee Schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff based on foundation capital (minimum capital B/.10,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization of the settlor's passport, power of attorney, banker's reference, and corporate existence certificate (estimated batch of five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería de Panamá), plus consular fees in the jurisdiction of origin where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fee per document (approximately USD 30–50 per document) plus consular legalization service fee where mandatory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the Foundation with the Public Registry (inscripción de la fundación)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff for Private Interest Foundations under Article 35 of Law 25 of 1995

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial filing of the UBO Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) / UAF Beneficial Ownership Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Online filing fee for initial UBO declaration under Executive Decree No. 299 of 2020

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent appointment for the initial incorporation term
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian resident agent (law firm / licensed agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard for first-year professional resident agent services, including registered office facility, mail handling, and statutory records custody

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative and professional paralegal assembly fee (pre-incorporation due diligence file compilation, statutory forms, bilingual Spanish/English drafting, and submission management)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Time-based fee at prevailing market rate (ranging USD 150–350 per hour, fixed at a capped package)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Private Interest Foundations Law, Law 25 of 12 June 1995, as amended by Law 63 of 2015; specifically Articles 2–8, 11, 12 and 29; together with the Registry General Regulations governing legal persons in the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), General Directorate of Legal Persons, Foundations and Trusts Section.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Constitution of a Private Interest Foundation (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Private Interest Foundation has no statutory minimum share capital. The foundation charter must specify the initial endowment (commonly US$10,000 or more) allocated to foundation assets. No escrow or deposit of funds in a Panamanian bank is legally mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 of the Foundation Council of [Foundation Name], adopted on [date] in Panama City. The Foundation Council resolves: (1) to accept the Founder's subscription of the initial endowment of US$10,000 and to approve the Foundation Charter as set forth in the Public Deed registered with the Public Registry of Panama; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address], Panama City; (3) to elect [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer; (4) to appoint [Name] of [law firm] as Resident Agent; and (5) to instruct the Resident Agent to procure the RUC, municipal operating notice, and all sanitary and environmental permits required for the food-manufacturing business. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Public Notary (Notary Public of the Circuit) in the Province of Panama.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to prepare the foundation charter in Spanish, including the founder's contribution, purpose clause, foundation council members, registered office, and resident agent appointment. Execute the deed before a Notary Public after verifying the identity and capacity of the founder and council members.
required_dossiers: Foundation charter draft
Copy of founder's passport
Proof of initial endowment or declaration of assets
Registered office address in Panama valid for a registered agent
Identification documents of appointed foundation council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing attorney identifies a defect, amend the draft by executing an addendum to the public deed and re-notarize the corrected text before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – General Directorate of Legal Persons, Foundations and Trusts Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the fully executed notarial public deed, together with the required copies, to the Public Registry of Panama. Pay the statutory inscription fee and stamp taxes. Wait for the Registry to complete legal review and issue the Certificate of Inscription (Certificado de Inscripción).
required_dossiers: Executed original and duplicates of the Public Deed of Incorporation
Receipt of payment of notarial fees and stamp taxes
Standard cover sheet and filing request form of the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of deficiency or 'reforma', correct the observations in writing and resubmit the clarified certificate within the granted term, ordinarily five working days, or file an administrative appeal before the Registry Directorate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, through the e-RUC online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation for Panamanian tax purposes using the RUC application form on the DGI portal. Attach the certified copy of the registered public deed and submit income tax, VAT (ITBMS), and employer registration declarations as applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the foundation public deed as registered
Identity documents of foundation council members
Proof of registered office address
Tax agent appointment letter if applicable
Completed DGI RUC application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is queried, rectify the digital ancillary documents, obtain updated certified copies from the Public Registry, and re-submit through the DGI portal. An in-person executive review at DGI can be requested in case of continued rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Aviso de Operación and Local Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama – Office of Commercial Operations and Municipal Licenses (Dirección de Avisos y Operación).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal business declaration form identifying the foundation as operator of a canned food manufacturing plant. Declare the nature of the industrial activity, registered office, and expected employees. Pay the municipal calculated tax based on declared capital and obtain the Aviso de Operación certificate.
required_dossiers: Registered foundation deed (certified copy)
RUC inscription certificate
Proof of lease or ownership of registered office and manufacturing facility
Certificate of municipal tax status
Identity document of legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues an objection due to inconsistent activity classification, amend the business category and resubmit the corrected declaration within ten business days. Further disputes may be referred to the Municipal Revenue Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Sanitary Registration and Environmental Impact Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Health (MINSA) – General Directorate of Public Health, National Food Safety Directorate; Ministry of Environment (MiAMBIENTE) – Environmental Classification and Evaluation Directorate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the food processing establishment for MINSA evaluation, including facility floor plans, aseptic treatment protocols, HACCP plan, product labeling, and sterilization records. Simultaneously file a Category II Preliminary Environmental Impact Assessment (EIAP) with MiAMBIENTE before commencement of manufacturing operations.
required_dossiers: RUC and registered foundation documents
Detailed product formulas and process flow diagrams
Label and packaging drafts for canned boba tapioca pearls
HACCP plan and sanitation standard operating procedures
Facility floor plan and aseptic filling line certifications
MiAMBIENTE environmental impact assessment application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MINSA or MiAMBIENTE issues technical observations, address each observation with revised plans and resubmit within fifteen working days. In the case of denial, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the respective superior authority within five days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health (MINSA) – National Food Safety Directorate; Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) – Directorate of Industry for industrial classification; and Ministry of Environment (MiAMBIENTE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Alimentos Procesados (processed food health registration) and the Municipal Aviso de Operación (business operating notice) for industrial food manufacturing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Panama Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Preliminary Environmental Impact Assessment (EIAP) for a small/medium food-processing plant producing canned boba tapioca pearls; a full Environmental Impact Study (EIA) may be required if the facility is large-scale or has significant wastewater loads.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Executive Decree No. 42 of 2001 for wastewater discharge, including limits for BOD, COD, pH, total suspended solids, oils and greases; National Air Quality Regulations under Executive Decree No. 5 of 2009 for VOC and particulate emissions; non-hazardous solid waste handling per Law 151 of 2017 and its regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering the manufacturing plant; structural load inspection certificate from a licensed civil engineer; and workplace occupational safety and health clearance from the Ministry of Labor (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral, MITRADEL) for machinery, ventilation, and employee exposure limits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP) — Panama's consolidated revenue administration (successor of the Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI, and the former National Customs Authority, ANA; consolidated under Law 365 of 2023, fully operational in 2024). Official portal: https://anip.gob.pa — hosts RUC registration, electronic filing, e-invoicing validation, and export declaration processing; legacy portal: www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with non-resident founder/beneficiaries: (1) execute the foundation deed before a Panamanian notary, appoint a licensed resident agent, and inscribe the foundation in the Registro Público de Panamá with a declared initial patrimony of at least B/10,000 (statutory minimum capital, no immediate funding requirement); pay the annual B/300 foundation franchise fee; (2) apply to ANIP for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente, the unified TIN/VAT ID replacing the former NIT) by filing the Solicitud de Inscripción de Contribuyente via the ANIP e-portal, attaching the certified copy of the registered foundation deed, the resident agent's notarized power of attorney, passport copies of founder and administrator, and a sworn declaration of territorial business activity (ISIC 1030 preserved-food manufacturing and export); (3) ANIP issues the RUC and, upon declaration of taxable supplies, simultaneously opens the ITBMS registration; (4) obtain the Firma Digital (digital signature) from the Autoridad Nacional para la Innovación Gubernamental (AIG) and enrol in ANIP's Facturación Electrónica system, configuring the zero-rated export invoice template; (5) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación, MINSA sanitary and food-plant registration for the canning facility, and the MICI export-visa registration. Practical lead time: 10–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama is a source-based taxation jurisdiction (Código Fiscal Art. 694); only Panamanian-source income is assessable. The PIF is a distinct juridical person for tax purposes; a foundation restricted to asset holding, investments, or estate administration sits outside income-tax assessment (only the annual B/300 public-registry fee and ITBMS registration duties apply). Where the PIF operates the canned-boba manufacturing plant, its manufacturing margin is Panamanian-source corporate income taxed at the 25% standard rate regardless of export destination; export sales are zero-rated only for ITBMS, not for corporate income tax sourcing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate U.S.-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections. Positive statutory elections available to the PIF: (i) in the foundation charter, elect non-commercial objects (passive, tax-quiescent profile) versus commercial manufacturing objects (activating territorial income-tax obligations); (ii) elect voluntary ITBMS registration before the first taxable transaction to accelerate input-credit recovery on production capex (retort and aseptic packaging lines); (iii) elect the simplified Pequeño Contribuyente ITBMS regime when annual gross turnover does not exceed B/36,000 — normally suboptimal for exporters because input credits are forfeited; (iv) elect among the ANIP-approved methods for the annual corporate income tax anticipo (advance payment). No D/NI or hybrid-entity elections exist under the territorial rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) – Panama’s sole banking and trust regulatory authority; no formal central bank exists, and the economy is fully dollarized
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized financial system with no exchange controls. The US dollar is legal tender, and the Panamanian balboa exists only as a token coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity. Capital and current account transactions are freely convertible and remittable, with no repatriation restrictions. Profit remittance, dividends, and royalty payments are subject only to standard territorial tax compliance and are otherwise freely transferable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion requirement for export proceeds. Panamanian exporters may retain and disburse USD export receipts freely, without any sovereign timeline or percentage-based conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to moderate. Panama does not maintain a bespoke fintech EMI or e-money institutional license. Offshore digital EMIs may only operate using a collection or payment gateway arrangement with a fully licensed local bank, and a private interest foundation (PIF) will usually face enhanced onboarding scrutiny when relying solely on non-resident digital EMI platforms due to the foundation’s hybrid identity structure. Legal viability is therefore limited without a local bank sponsor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the foundation’s founders, council members, and ultimate beneficial owner is generally required at account opening. While a limited number of Panamanian banks permit remote documentary onboarding for low-risk operating companies, a PIF will typically trigger a mandatory in-person interview for all beneficial owners and executive council members. Original foundation deed, apostilled certificate of good standing, and notarized identification are standard prerequisites.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation has nominee council members or beneficial owner information is obscured by foundation governance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Foundation Deed with express beneficiary designation, notarized beneficial ownership declaration, current certificate of incumbency, minutes of the foundation council approving banking account opening, and registry excerpt from the Public Registry of Panama confirming foundation existence and current council members.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident economic substance and lack of physical corporate presence in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified business plan describing boba tapioca manufacturing operations, lease or service agreement with a Panama-based registered agent, payroll or contractor evidence if staff is maintained, tax authority registration, and audited or CPA-compiled financial statements demonstrating real commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds consists of initial capital injection from a foreign jurisdiction without clear upstream origin
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering at least twelve months for the funding entity, source of wealth declaration signed by the beneficial owner, certified copies of commercial contracts or invoices supporting the business purpose, and an independent legal opinion confirming the legality of the funds in the originating jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the parent or beneficial owner’s bank directly to the PIF’s Panama account. The wire must carry a clear reference to the PIF’s name and account number, and should indicate a purpose code consistent with a capital contribution, such as 'CIP' or 'Capital Injection'. No exchange control approval is required, but the receiving Panamanian bank may ask for a certified copy of the foundation deed and a notarized resolution of the foundation council authorizing the injection, along with a source-of-funds narrative to satisfy AML/KYC standards.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for ingredient import, aseptic packaging equipment, and raw tapioca starch should be settled by TT wire transfer using SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, or by commercial letter of credit (at sight or usance) governed by UCP 600. When panama-clearing banks need nostro liquidity, underlying payments are routed through the US correspondent banking network using Fedwire or CHIPS. Documentary collection and direct MT103 payments are the most practicable rails, while commercial LCs provide enhanced security for larger capital machinery purchases.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards on USD against non-USD currencies for import invoice hedging
Cross-currency swaps between USD and major hard currencies for operational settlement
Over-the-counter FX forward contracts executed with a licensed Panamanian bank or global bank counterparty
Plain-vanilla FX call and put options with collar structures to protect against adverse non-USD supplier currency moves

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) / National Treasury (Dirección General de Ingresos), payable via Banco Nacional de Panamá or authorized online payment portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar deadline of June 30 of each calendar year, irrespective of incorporation anniversary; standard fee is US$350 for an indefinite-duration PIF, reduced to US$100 only for a PIF with a fixed duration of ten years or less
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Payment made July 1–September 30 attracts a 10% surcharge; October 1–December 31 attracts a US$200 surcharge; January 1–April 30 of the following year attracts a US$500 surcharge; non-payment beyond April 30 results in loss of Good Standing certificates, administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings ordered by the Public Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Update and Compliance Confirmation (Ley 70 de 2019, Executive Decree No. 13 of 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry — Beneficial Ownership Database (administered through the registered agent's online portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days following the anniversary of the PIF's registration in the Public Registry, and additionally within 30 days of any change in the beneficial owner, foundation member, or council member
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual confirmation or accurate UBO updates exposes the foundation to administrative fines ranging from US$100 to US$5,000, adverse notations of non-compliance in the Public Registry, deactivation of standing status, and potential strike-off; persistent breach shifts personal liability to Foundation Council members for foundation obligations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a Private Interest Foundation solely at incorporation; independent audit becomes compulsory when (i) the Foundation Charter or Regulations expressly mandate audited statements, (ii) the PIF earns Panamanian-source business income requiring DGI registration, in which case audited financial statements are required once annual gross income exceeds US$3,000,000, or (iii) a bank, investor, or AML due-diligence process under Ley 70/2019 requires audited financials as a condition of financing or account opening
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the accepted professional standard in Panama and is preferred by the Dirección General de Ingresos; local commercial bookkeeping rules under the Código de Comercio and customary Panamanian local GAAP also apply to domestic books; all statutory records must be maintained in United States dollars, the official monetary unit in Panama

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must obtain, verify, and continuously maintain beneficial ownership information; annually, within 30 days after the PIF's registration anniversary, the agent files a confirmation or 'no-change' declaration with the Public Registry Beneficial Ownership Database; any transfer of founder rights, member units, or beneficial interests must be reported within 30 days of the transfer; the confirmation certifies that the recorded beneficial owner is current, accurate, and complete, and failure to confirm subjects both the agent and the foundation to administrative fines and loss of Good Standing
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Members (Libro de Registro de Miembros)
Foundation Council Minutes Book (Registro de Actas del Consejo de Fundación)
Foundation Charter and Regulations, together with duly protocoled amendments and resolutions
Beneficial ownership information file maintained by the registered agent under Ley 70 de 2019

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,000 – US$3,000 per annum for a licensed Panama registered agent, including statutory representation, processing of the annual franchise tax, annual UBO confirmation filing, and issuance of Good Standing certificates
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 – US$7,500 for a certified independent audit of a low-activity PIF, incurred only when triggered by charter mandate, banking covenants, or Panamanian-source income above the US$3,000,000 threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% (standard ISR); 10% surcharge on net taxable income exceeding B/.1,500,000 (USD 1,500,000) yields 27.5% marginal rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source system: income derived from business activities performed outside Panama and from assets located abroad is exempt. Panama-source canned-boba manufacturing profits taxed at 25%/27.5%. Preferential items: free-zone manufacturing (ISR exemption on export profits), agro-industrial incentives under Ley 41 de 2007, SEM regional headquarters regime at 5%, and export-relevant deductible ITBMS (7%) for registered exporters.
